questions: How many devices did you measure, and how many showed the global signatures and the zero-bias peaks? Page 4 says the global features appear "in all examined devices" and p. 5 gives a tunnel junction yield below 50%, but the number of devices examined isn't stated.
Why were the other devices set aside, for example devices with a single working tunnel probe other than device A?

Which ranges did you measure beyond the ones shown: field angle, negative Bx for the correlation analysis, temperature, both field sweep directions for the half-flux jumps (p. 4 says the high-field jumps depend on sweep direction), and device A gate voltages (the Fig. S1 caption lists VG = −10, 0, 20 V while the panels read 0, 10 and 20 V)?
What does the second-best device or dataset look like? Device C appears in Figs. S2 and S3; were there cooldowns or gate settings of device A where the zero-bias peak did not appear at half flux?

For the end-to-end analysis in Fig. 4l and Fig. S3l, how did you compute the third derivative (smoothing, bias window, resolution), what fraction of correlated peaks would uncorrelated signs give, and how does the fraction move when those choices change?

In device C, Supp. p. 4 says a zero-bias peak "was mostly absent in this device", while Supp. p. 5 reports "a strong increase of correlated zero-bias conductance peaks" in the first expected topological regime. Which gate voltages does each statement cover?
What are the tunnel resistances of TJ1 and TJ2 in each device? Methods give "resistances exceeding 100 kΩ" (p. 5), while Fig. S1a shows G of about 0.6 to 1.4 e²/h at 2 mV, roughly 18 to 43 kΩ.

Would a two-junction interferometer with unequal arms and skewed current-phase relations, and no topological surface states, give the same Ic(Φ) and the same η sign reversal at half-integer flux as Figs. 1e and 3a? Which feature of your data would differ?
